  Requirement: "Gate only this new admission behind the env var REVIEW_SANDBOX_ADMIT_CHATGPT_POOL_CONFIG_ENABLED. It defaults to true, and the value false turns it off." (Linked issue #9111.) The same requirement is restated in "Ship the new behaviour on: gate only the new code path behind REVIEW_SANDBOX_ADMIT_CHATGPT_POOL_CONFIG_ENABLED as an off switch. Unset, empty or `true` (any case) keeps it on; `false` turns it off; any other value also turns it off and logs a warning."
  Expected change site: `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml` environment wiring for the review sandbox prepare step (and matching `vars` -> `env:` mapping if the intent is operator-controllability), so the operator can set `false` and have the admission actually disable.
  Evidence of absence: `chatgpt_pool_config_admitted()` in `scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:150-164` reads `os.environ.get(CHATGPT_POOL_CONFIG_FLAG)`. The flag appears only in the helper (scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:146), the changelog fragment, the agents fragment and the tests. `scripts/review_untrusted_sandbox.sh` (the only normal caller — it invokes `python3 .../review_untrusted_workspace.py snapshot` at line 105 and `transfer` at lines 653 and 861) never exports the flag, and `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml` (lines 3660, 3668, 3671, 3818, 3820) never sets it either. In real runs the helper always takes the unset/empty branch, so `false` cannot turn the admission off through the documented operator path. The agents fragment itself states the gap ("review_autofix.yml does not forward a repository variable for it, so a repository variable alone does not reach the helper").
